**ORBITAL – Intelligent Astronaut Health Monitoring System**

ORBITAL is an interactive health monitoring platform designed to monitor astronauts' physical and physiological health during space missions. It tracks important health parameters such as heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature, sleep patterns, stress levels, exercise activity, and radiation exposure.

The system provides individual crew health profiles, readiness scores, interactive health visualizations, and 30-day health trend analysis. It also identifies potential health risks and provides personalized self-care recommendations and countermeasures.

ORBITAL includes a Solar Particle Event emergency simulator to demonstrate radiation-related alerts and astronaut safety procedures.

Our goal is to support astronaut health monitoring, early risk identification, and informed health management during long-duration space missions.
details:
ORBITAL – Intelligent Astronaut Health Monitoring System

ORBITAL is an interactive astronaut health monitoring platform designed to support the monitoring of crew health during space missions, especially long-duration missions. It provides a centralized dashboard where users can view individual astronaut profiles and monitor important health parameters, including heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature, sleep patterns, stress levels, exercise activity, and radiation exposure.

The system presents health information through interactive charts, 30-day health trends, readiness scores, and health-system analysis panels. It helps identify potential health risks by displaying alerts and providing self-care recommendations and countermeasures. The platform also includes a Solar Particle Event emergency simulator to demonstrate radiation-related risks and astronaut safety procedures.

Benefits and Intended Impact:
ORBITAL aims to make astronaut health information easier to understand and monitor. By organizing multiple health indicators in one dashboard, it can help identify unusual changes, support early risk awareness, and assist astronauts and mission support teams in making informed health-management decisions. Its intended impact is to contribute to safer space missions and better health monitoring during extended human exploration of space.

Tools and Technologies Used:
The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Tailwind CSS was used for interface styling, Chart.js for interactive health data visualizations, and Lucide Icons for interface elements. The application was developed and tested using Visual Studio Code and a web browser.

Creativity and Innovation:
The project combines astronaut health monitoring, visual analytics, readiness scoring, personalized countermeasures, and emergency simulation in a single mission-control-style interface. Its futuristic dashboard design includes a holographic DNA visualization, glowing telemetry elements, and interactive health panels to make complex health information more engaging and understandable.

Factors Considered:
The project considers the challenges of monitoring astronaut health in space, including changes in sleep patterns, physical activity, cardiovascular indicators, stress, and radiation exposure. We also considered the importance of clear visual communication, easy navigation, individual crew profiles, early warning indicators, and practical recommendations. The platform is designed as a prototype using simulated health data and is intended to demonstrate how an integrated astronaut health monitoring system could work.
